A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same REGENT study with complete Sections 1–7 and Appendices A–E. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish that the equations, figures and tables, including the rotated Table 1, are available for reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original policy evaluations across robotics and game environments in Section 6, with ablations, runtime measurements and detailed experimental results in Appendices C–D.

after.justification: v2 retains these original policy evaluations, ablations, runtime measurements and supplementary results in Section 6 and Appendices C–D.

M1.justification: Sections 4.1–4.2 and Appendix A retain identical R&P retrieval, 19-neighbor transformer context, distance-weighted interpolation, architectures and training losses. No method component or procedure changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Metaworld, Mujoco, Atari, BabyAI and ProcGen coverage, including held-out environments and unseen ProcGen levels. No training or evaluation task, domain or scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the corresponding experiments: R&P, JAT/Gato variants, RAG and finetuning variants, behavior cloning and DRIL in Figure 4/Table 1; the Mujoco comparators in Figure 13/Table 2; and MTT in Figure 5/Table 7.

E3.justification: Sections 4 and 6 and Appendix A retain the same data selections, preprocessing, model sizes, training budgets, demonstration counts, normalized-return metrics and sticky-action evaluation settings. No protocol is added or revised.

E4.justification: The interpolation analysis, context-length and ordering ablations, distance-metric comparison, runtime measurements, qualitative examples and unseen-level evaluations are unchanged, including Figures 8–14 and Appendix D.

E5.justification: Figure 4/Table 1 and Figure 5/Table 7 retain the same three-training-seed reporting and standard deviations. Evaluation-rollout counts, seed information and the single-training-seed descriptions for ablations also remain unchanged.

E6.justification: The numerical entries, plotted results and qualitative findings are identical, including Tables 1–8. For example, Table 1 retains aggregate means of 0.602 for REGENT and 0.633 for REGENT Finetuned under the same settings.

T1.justification: The MDP formulation, Definition 5.1, Theorem 5.2 and Appendix B's lemma and proof are unchanged. No mathematical assumption, derivation or proof correction is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about retrieval enabling adaptation without finetuning and REGENT outperforming generalist baselines with smaller models and less pretraining data. Contribution scope and novelty claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: Both versions retain the same explanations of interpolation, retrieval and distance-metric behavior. The limitations concerning new embodiments, long-horizon environments and generalization beyond the training suites remain unchanged in Section 7 and the appendices.

D1.justification: Appendix A retains identical architectural hyperparameters, optimizer settings, retrieval preparation and baseline training recipes. The reproducibility statement, code-availability information and external link destinations are also unchanged.

R1.justification: The references and research positioning in Section 2 and Appendix E are unchanged, including comparisons with JAT/Gato, MTT and other retrieval or in-context learning approaches.

P1.justification: The running header changes from 'Under review' to 'Published' at ICLR 2025. Three instances of 'demos' become 'demonstrations' on pages 7–9, and 'for the above' is removed from an Appendix A pointer. Section and appendix organization remain identical.

P2.justification: The updated header and first-page arXiv version/date stamp produce small visual changes, with limited prose reflow on pages 7–9. Figures 1–19 and Tables 1–8 retain identical displays, captions and placement.

improvement.justification: v2 makes publication-status updates and very small wording and typesetting edits. The methods, empirical evidence, theoretical arguments, reproducibility information and limitations remain unchanged throughout the main paper and appendices. These cosmetic changes produce no meaningful net difference in overall paper quality.
